title: Claude can run the threads. You still pick the goal.
friendlyTitle: Claude can run several jobs at once. You still choose the goal.
summary: Anthropic is rolling out redesigned Claude Code projects in beta. You set a goal and the repositories. A coordinator splits the work into threads, and each thread is a cloud Claude Code session on its own branch. You can watch or steer from the project chat, including from a phone, and the work can continue after you leave the computer. Access starts with selected Pro and Max users who already use cloud sessions and do not have existing web or desktop projects.
friendlySummary: Anthropic is testing a new kind of Claude Code project with some paying users. You name the goal and the code. Claude splits the work into separate jobs, each on its own copy of the code. You can check in from your phone, and the jobs can keep going after you close the laptop.
whyItMatters: This is for work that takes more than one reply. Shared memory is meant to carry decisions across threads, so you do not re-explain the project each time. Several full sessions also use up the allowance faster. Overlapping edits still land as ordinary merge conflicts. Local threads, on your own machine, are not in this beta. Team and Enterprise plans come later.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Use it for work that takes longer than one answer. The project is meant to remember earlier decisions, so you do not have to repeat them. Several jobs at once also use your allowance faster. If two jobs edit the same code, you still have to sort out the clash. This test is not on your own computer yet.
